guides.title: Getting Hardware Set Up
guides.overview: Hardware Setup is Page 0 — the gating page. Every other mode (Jog, Calibration, Print Builder, Printing, Workflows) stays locked in the sidebar until this page reports a valid config; only Hardware Setup and Settings are always reachable. The page is a row of sub-pages (Device, Identity, Plate, Rosette, Ink, Needle, Pump, Cameras, Xbox Controller) with a persistent left-edge control panel (Connect Hardware + Jog Stages + Live Position) that stays visible on every sub-page. An operator uses it once per machine to describe the physical rig (connect stages, calibrate steppers, set the Z datum/direction/limits, calibrate pump plungers, record the safety envelope, set feedrates, pick/design the plate, define inks/needle, calibrate cameras) and again per experiment to pick the plate/inks/needle. A config becomes valid when a needle gauge is selected, at least one pump is enabled with a syringe, every enabled pump has at least one ink, the plate format (or custom-plate file) is recognized, and each needle channel maps to a unique enabled pump.
guides.where_to_find: Sidebar → first icon "Hardware Setup" (always enabled, even on a fresh launch). Inside, switch sub-pages via the top tab strip in this order: Device · Identity · Plate · Rosette · Ink · Needle · Pump · Cameras · Xbox Controller. The Connect Hardware / Jog Stages / Live Position panel is docked on the far left and is shared across all sub-pages.
prerequisites: Physical rig wired and powered: Prior ProScan XY box on, Marlin Z+pumps board on USB, optional Xbox controller, microscope + needle cameras plugged in.
Know your hardware: needle gauge/length, syringe volume per pump, and which physical Marlin axis (X/Y/Z/E) drives each logical axis (Z, P1, P2, P3) on your wiring.
On ME3B V1 the needle DESCENDS as raw Z increases — do not assume up=larger Z. The Z Axis Setup derives the true up-direction for you; just jog to the real mechanical extremes when prompted.
You can do the whole walkthrough in Simulate mode (no hardware) to learn the page; calibration values captured in simulation are not physically meaningful.

Camera µm/px, objective calibrations, image correction, and role→camera assignments persist per physical camera (by device identity) in a per-machine store, so they survive setup-file loads and restarts independently of the hardware config.

steps.title: Connect the stages (or simulate)
steps.detail: In the left Connect Hardware card, click Connect on XY stage and on Z + Pumps (or Simulate for the built-in simulator, no hardware). Optionally Connect the Xbox controller. Badges read Not connected → Connecting…/Starting simulator… → Connected or Simulated; a red Failed/Error means the port didn't open. The Disconnect (×) button tears a device down so you can switch real↔simulator. On a real ZP connect the app caches the COM port and ~1 s later auto-runs a Marlin alignment check.

steps.title: Pick a device profile (Device sub-page)
steps.detail: Open Device. At the top, choose a Profile (ships with Standard / Conservative) and click Load to populate every section below with that machine's saved values, or Save As… to create your own. The profile bundles safety limits, feedrates, axis map, steps/mm, Z setup, plate orientation, and pump calibration.

steps.title: Set the axis mapping
steps.detail: In Axis Mapping, set which physical Marlin axis (X/Y/Z/E) drives each logical axis (Z, P1, P2, P3). Defaults are Z→X, P1→Y, P2→Z, P3→E. Click Save Mapping to push it to the live ZP stage and persist to settings + the active profile.

steps.title: Calibrate XY motion
steps.detail: In XY Stage Calibration set Velocity (% max), Acceleration, and optional Jerk, and click Save XY Calibration (sends to ProScan + persists). Optionally use the report-only Units verification row (Axis · Distance · Move · Measured · Compare) to confirm 1:1 travel.

steps.title: Calibrate steppers and feedrates (ZP Stage Calibration)
steps.detail: Pick an axis, enter a Commanded distance, click Move + / Move − at a chosen Feedrate, measure the real travel, enter the Measured distance, and click Calculate & Send M92. Use Invert Direction to flip an axis sign. Raise the feedrate and test until you find a safe ceiling, then Record as Max. Set per-axis max accel, then Save Calibration (sends M92/M201). Check alignment compares Marlin (M503) against the profile and turns mismatched axes red. You can also click any steps/mm or max-feedrate cell to edit it directly.

steps.title: Run the Z Axis Setup (datum + direction + limits)
steps.detail: Using the left jog pad, drive the needle ALL THE WAY DOWN, then click 1 · Set Bottom (Z = 0). Jog ALL THE WAY UP and click 2 · Set Top. The controller derives the up-direction (z_up_sign) and the Z soft-limit envelope automatically; status turns green. Optionally set the three Standard plate offsets (mm below the needle-cam fiducial) and Save offsets. Tick 'Plate mounted 180° to stage' if A1 should display top-left with stage 0,0 bottom-right (default ON for ME3B V1) — re-teach plate calibration after changing it.

steps.title: Calibrate each pump plunger (Pump Plunger Setup)
steps.detail: On the Device sub-page (right under the Z block, one block per P1/P2/P3): jog the plunger ALL THE WAY IN (syringe empty) and click 1 · Set Dispensed (empty, fill 0); jog ALL THE WAY OUT (full) and click 2 · Set Aspirated (full), then confirm in the dialog. This derives and OWNS the aspirate/dispense direction and saves the pump soft-limit extents. Green status confirms the derived sign and capacity.

steps.title: Record the XY/Z/pump safety envelope
steps.detail: In Jog & Safety Limits the jog pad bypasses soft limits so you can find the mechanical extremes. For each axis row, jog to an extreme and click ⤓ Set Min / ⤒ Set Max to stamp the current position into the spinboxes; ⊙ Set Zero re-stamps a zero reference. Leave 'Enable safety limits' on. Click Save Safety Limits & Zero to push the envelope to the live controller and persist.

steps.title: Set ZP feedrates and apply everything
steps.detail: In ZP Stage Feedrates (% of Z max) set Max/Retract/Insert/Jog as percentages of the Z max you recorded; the live mm/min is shown next to each. Click Save Feedrates. Use Override / Sync Axis Position only to recover position after a ZP power cycle. Finally click Apply Settings at the bottom to commit the whole Device page in one go.

steps.title: Name the setup (Identity)
steps.detail: On Identity, type a Name (becomes the save filename) and optional Notes. The Saved setups list shows every config in config/hardware/ — select one and click Load Setup (or double-click) to apply a whole accessory setup (plate/inks/needle/pumps/cameras).

steps.title: Choose or design the plate (Plate)
steps.detail: On Plate, pick a bundled format (● 6/12/24/48/96/384) or a saved custom plate (○) from the picker, or design one with Select/Single-Well/Grid/Circle-Pattern/Line/Construction-Line/Dimension tools plus constraints, then New / Save / Save As… / Delete. Fit reframes the view; Snap toggles 1 mm drag snapping; Wheel zoom toggles scroll-wheel zoom; Dim ref switches new dimensions between well center and edge.

steps.title: Design rosette sub-wells (Rosette, optional)
steps.detail: On Rosette, double-click a well to drill into it and design its sub-wells (which flatten into A1.a, A1.b… and become first-class wells). It shares the plate design with the Plate page; Save plate delegates to the Plate page save. A legacy Rosette Library (Add/Edit/Remove) of RosetteInsert presets is also available.

steps.title: Build the Ink Library + reagent locations (Ink)
steps.detail: On Ink, click Add Ink — set Name, Well type (ink/wash/buffer/waste/oil), optional Ink subtype (enabled only for 'ink'), Viscosity/Granule Ø/Cell Ø/Density, and Color; Edit/Remove manage rows. In Reagent Locations, pick a reagent then click wells on the plate view and click Assign selected to pin it (well fill = ink color, outline = type color). Service types are excluded from the per-pump ink checklist automatically.

steps.title: Configure the needle and channel mapping (Needle)
steps.detail: On Needle, pick the Gauge (info line shows ID/OD/Wall in µm), Length (1.0/1.5/2.0"), and number of Channels (1–3). In Needle Channel Assignment, map each channel to a unique enabled pump; the status reads ✓ All channels assigned when complete.

steps.title: Set up pumps and timing (Pump)
steps.detail: On Pump, Enable each used pump, pick its Syringe (volume), Mode (Incremental/Continuous), and check the inks it can aspirate from the printable-ink list. The summary shows P1→[…] assignments. Under Pump Timing (all pumps) set the global Settle time and Prime time.

steps.title: Detect, assign, and calibrate cameras (Cameras)
steps.detail: On Cameras, click Detect Cameras (or Load Cameras to restore + start a saved setup). For each slot pick a Source and a Role (Microscope / Needle X-view / Needle Y-view — singletons), click ▶ Start to verify the live feed, and tune Brightness/Contrast/Gamma under the preview. Calibrate µm/px… on each needle camera and add+calibrate objectives in Objective Calibration Setup. Click Save Camera Settings to make it this machine's startup default.

steps.title: Confirm valid + save
steps.detail: Watch the Setup Status banner: ⚠ lines list what's missing; ✓ Setup complete means the config is valid and the sidebar unlocks every page. Click Save Config to write the hardware config to disk (config/hardware/).

settings.name: XY stage / Z+Pumps / Xbox: Connect
settings.what_it_does: Opens the real serial connection to that device (Prior ProScan XY, Marlin Z+pumps board, Xbox controller). Badge goes Connecting… → Connected.
settings.recommendation: Connect both stages before any jog/calibration. ZP connect also caches the COM port and runs a Marlin alignment check ~1 s later.

settings.name: XY stage / Z+Pumps: Simulate
settings.what_it_does: Opens the built-in software simulator for that device instead of real hardware — no app restart needed.
settings.recommendation: Use to learn the page or test without hardware; badge reads Simulated. Calibration captured in sim is not physically meaningful.

settings.name: Disconnect (×) per device
settings.what_it_does: Tears down the current stage/controller so you can switch between real and simulator or re-open.
settings.recommendation: Use before switching a device between Connect and Simulate.

settings.name: Jog Stages: jog pad (XY pad / Z buttons / pump buttons + step selectors)
settings.what_it_does: Drives each stage manually. On Hardware Setup this jog runs in setup mode: soft-limit clamping and the pump-enabled check are bypassed so you can reach mechanical extremes (a yellow banner warns of this).
settings.recommendation: Watch the Live Position bars — markers ring red past the recorded envelope. Z▲ retracts (height-frame up), following the taught z_up_sign.

settings.name: Jog Stages → Speeds: XY / Z / P
settings.what_it_does: Per-axis jog speed: XY in µm/s (applied to ProScan via SMS on each jog), Z and pumps in mm/min feedrate.
settings.default: Seeded to half of the calibrated max on first settings load; spinbox defaults XY 2000 µm/s, Z 600 mm/min, P 200 mm/min
settings.recommendation: Leave near default; each spinbox max is capped at the calibrated max. A manual edit is preserved across reloads.

settings.name: Jog Stages → Refresh Positions
settings.what_it_does: Forces a fresh, uncached position read from each connected stage into the Live Position readouts.
settings.recommendation: Use after a jog if the readout looks stale.

settings.name: Live Position (X/Y/Z/P1/P2/P3 bars + readouts)
settings.what_it_does: Shows each axis position vs its safety-limit envelope. Z reads in the unified user frame (0=bottom datum, up=+). A calibrated pump reads as fill in µL (0=empty→capacity=full) with raw mm in the tooltip; uncalibrated pumps read raw mm.
settings.recommendation: A red ring on a marker means the axis is outside the recorded envelope.

settings.name: Device → Device Profile (combo + Load / Save / Save As… / Delete / Refresh)
settings.what_it_does: Loads/saves a physical-machine settings bundle (safety limits, feedrates, axis map, steps/mm, Z setup, plate orientation, pump calibration) to config/hardware/devices/<name>.json. Load applies it to every section below.
settings.recommendation: Save your own profile per machine so the calibration travels with the rig regardless of which experiment config is loaded.

settings.name: Device → Axis Mapping (Z/P1/P2/P3 → X/Y/Z/E) + Save Mapping
settings.what_it_does: Maps each logical axis to the physical Marlin axis that drives it on your wiring. Save Mapping pushes to the live ZP stage and persists to settings + the active profile.
settings.recommendation: Set this to match how your steppers are physically wired before calibrating steps/mm.

settings.name: Device → XY Stage Calibration: Velocity (% max)
settings.what_it_does: ProScan SMS — max XY velocity as a percentage of the controller's hardware ceiling.
settings.recommendation: Leave at 100% unless you want gentler XY motion.

settings.name: Device → XY Stage Calibration: Acceleration
settings.what_it_does: ProScan SAS acceleration as a percentage (1–100).
settings.recommendation: Default is fine for most rigs.

settings.name: Device → XY Stage Calibration: Jerk (optional)
settings.what_it_does: ProScan SCS jerk; silently ignored if the controller protocol doesn't declare set_jerk. 0 = leave the controller default.
settings.recommendation: Leave 0 unless you have a reason to tune it.

settings.name: Device → XY Stage Calibration: Units verification (Axis / Distance / Move / Measured / Compare)
settings.what_it_does: Report-only check: command a distance on X or Y, measure with a caliper, enter it, Compare shows deviation %. No value is auto-corrected.
settings.recommendation: ProScan moves natively at 1:1; a >1% deviation flags a mechanical issue, not a software fix.

settings.name: Device → XY Stage Calibration: Save XY Calibration
settings.what_it_does: Sends velocity/acceleration/jerk to ProScan and persists to settings + the active device profile.
settings.recommendation: Click after editing velocity/acceleration/jerk.

settings.name: Device → ZP Stage Calibration: Axis / Commanded distance / Move +/− / Feedrate
settings.what_it_does: Sends a known-distance ZP move (Z or pump) in either direction at the chosen feedrate (bypasses soft limits — setup mode) so you can measure real travel and probe the max feedrate.
settings.default: Commanded 1.0 mm, Feedrate 600 mm/min (seeds from the axis's recorded max when you switch axis)
settings.recommendation: Lower the feedrate if the motor stalls or skips steps.

settings.name: Device → ZP Stage Calibration: Measured distance / Calculate & Send M92
settings.what_it_does: Computes new steps/mm = current × (commanded ÷ measured) and sends M92 to Marlin, persisting to settings + the device profile.
settings.recommendation: Measure the actual physical movement precisely; this sets the axis's true scale.

settings.name: Device → ZP Stage Calibration: Invert Direction
settings.what_it_does: Negates the saved steps/mm for the selected axis — flips which way 'positive' moves on Marlin without changing step magnitude.
settings.recommendation: Use if an axis jogs the wrong way after calibration.

settings.name: Device → ZP Stage Calibration: Record as Max
settings.what_it_does: Saves the current feedrate as the experimentally-discovered max for the selected axis (device_profile.per_axis_max_feedrate).
settings.recommendation: Find a safe ceiling (no stall/skipped steps) before recording. The Z max feeds the ZP Feedrates percentages.

settings.name: Device → ZP Stage Calibration: max accel (mm/s²) per axis
settings.what_it_does: Per-axis max acceleration sent to Marlin via M201 on Save Calibration.
settings.recommendation: Keep Z low; default values are sensible.

settings.name: Device → ZP Stage Calibration: steps/mm & max feedrate cells (clickable)
settings.what_it_does: Read-only grid (columns Z/P1/P2/P3) of current steps/mm and max feedrate per axis; click any cell to edit it directly in a popup (sends M92/M203 + persists).
settings.recommendation: Quick edit path when you already know the value and don't need the move/measure workflow.

settings.name: Device → ZP Stage Calibration: Check alignment / Save Calibration
settings.what_it_does: Check alignment queries Marlin (M503) and turns mismatched axes red. Save Calibration re-sends steps/mm (M92), per-axis max accel (M201), and per-axis max feedrate, persisting to settings/profile.
settings.recommendation: Run Check alignment after edits; Save Calibration is a 'commit everything in this section' convenience.

settings.name: Device → Z Axis Setup: 1 · Set Bottom (Z = 0)
settings.what_it_does: Captures the raw Z with the needle jogged all the way DOWN and makes it the user-Z = 0 datum.
settings.recommendation: Jog fully down FIRST; this is the mechanical hard-bottom datum.

settings.name: Device → Z Axis Setup: 2 · Set Top
settings.what_it_does: Captures the raw Z with the needle all the way UP; the controller derives the up-direction (z_up_sign) and the Z soft-limit envelope automatically.
settings.recommendation: Jog far from bottom so the direction is unambiguous; status warns if they're too close.

settings.name: Device → Z Axis Setup: Standard plate offsets (Top / Bottom / Safe) + Save offsets
settings.what_it_does: Three offsets in mm BELOW the needle-cam fiducial; the Calibration page uses them to pre-fill plate-Z guesses. Save offsets persists to the device profile and pushes to the controller.
settings.recommendation: Tune to your plate geometry; Max/Replace Z stay manual.

settings.name: Device → Z Axis Setup: Plate mounted 180° to stage
settings.what_it_does: Single per-machine orientation switch: drives BOTH the 180° display flip on stage-frame plate views AND the plate-local→stage geometry sign (well A1 top-left, stage 0,0 bottom-right).
settings.default: ON when unset (default for ME3B V1)
settings.recommendation: Leave ON for ME3B V1. Re-teach plate calibration after changing it (a mismatch invalidates the taught XY calibration).

settings.name: Device → Jog & Safety Limits: Enable safety limits
settings.what_it_does: Master switch for the recorded soft-limit envelope across the whole app. (The setup jog pad bypasses it either way.)
settings.recommendation: Keep ON in normal operation; the envelope protects the needle/plate.

settings.name: Device → Per-axis position & safety limits: ⊙ Set Zero / ⤓ Set Min / ⤒ Set Max (X,Y,Z,P1,P2,P3)
settings.what_it_does: Set Zero stamps the current position as that axis's zero reference. Set Min/Set Max stamp the current position into the min/max spinbox. XY and pump store absolute raw; Z stores the unified user frame.
settings.default: X ±130000 µm, Y ±85000 µm, Z derived by setup (default spins −10/50), P ±50 mm
settings.recommendation: Jog to each true mechanical extreme before stamping; remember to Save.

settings.name: Device → Save Safety Limits & Zero
settings.what_it_does: Persists safety_limits + zero positions to settings and pushes them to the live StageController.
settings.recommendation: Click after recording min/max so the live envelope updates.

settings.name: Device → Pump Plunger Setup (P1/P2/P3): 1 · Set Dispensed (empty, fill 0)
settings.what_it_does: Captures the raw plunger position all the way IN (syringe empty) as the fill=0 datum.
settings.recommendation: Jog the plunger fully in first; this is the empty datum.

settings.name: Device → Pump Plunger Setup: 2 · Set Aspirated (full)
settings.what_it_does: Captures the plunger all the way OUT (full); after a confirm dialog, derives and OWNS the aspirate/dispense direction and sets the pump soft-limit extents.
settings.recommendation: Only confirm if the plunger is truly at its mechanical extremes (empty→full). Re-run per machine after a wiring change; a wrong sign reverses fluid flow.

settings.name: Device → Override / Sync Axis Position (Z/P1/P2/P3 → set to … + ⟳ Set Position)
settings.what_it_does: After a ZP power cycle (Marlin has no absolute encoder), enter where each axis physically is in zero-referenced mm and Set Position rebases the firmware counter via G92 — no motion.
settings.recommendation: Use only to recover position after a board power cycle; values are in the same mm frame as the Jog page, not the raw counter.

settings.name: Device → ZP Stage Feedrates (% of Z max): Max / Retract / Insert / Jog
settings.what_it_does: Each is a percentage of the Z-axis max feedrate; the live mm/min is shown next to each spin.
settings.recommendation: Set the Z max in ZP Stage Calibration first; then Save Feedrates (sends M203, updates retract/insert/jog).

settings.name: Device → ZP Stage Feedrates: Auto-save position to EEPROM
settings.what_it_does: When on, periodically saves position to the board's EEPROM (M500).
settings.recommendation: Leave off unless you specifically need persisted firmware position.

settings.name: Device → Save Feedrates
settings.what_it_does: Computes absolute mm/min from the percentages, persists to settings, sends M203 to Marlin for the max feedrate, and updates the controller's retract/insert/jog feedrates.
settings.recommendation: Click after editing the feedrate percentages.

settings.name: Device → Apply Settings / Reset to Defaults
settings.what_it_does: Apply commits every Device section at once (the per-section Save buttons do the same scoped). Reset discards unsaved edits and reloads the saved device profile.
settings.recommendation: Click Apply Settings after a full Device pass.

settings.name: Identity → Name / Notes
settings.what_it_does: Free-text setup name (becomes the save filename) and optional notes for this hardware config.
settings.recommendation: Name it after the experiment/accessory set so saved setups are easy to find.

settings.name: Identity → Saved setups list + Load Setup / Refresh
settings.what_it_does: Lists every saved hardware config in config/hardware/; Load Setup (or double-click) applies the selected one to every section (plate/inks/needle/pumps/cameras).
settings.recommendation: Use to swap whole accessory setups quickly.

settings.name: Plate → format/custom picker
settings.what_it_does: Selects the active well plate — a bundled standard (● 6/12/24/48/96/384) or a user-saved custom design (○). Drives the plate model the whole app uses.
settings.default: Loads 96-well on first open; config default 24
settings.recommendation: Pick the plate you'll actually print into; a custom plate must exist under config/hardware/plates/user/ to validate.

settings.name: Plate → designer tools (Select / Single Well / Grid Pattern / Circle Pattern / Line / Construction Line / Dimension)
settings.what_it_does: Parametric sketch tools to draw wells and impose constraints; output compiles to a WellPlate.
settings.recommendation: Only needed when authoring a custom plate; use bundled standards otherwise.

settings.name: Plate → New / Save / Save As… / Delete
settings.what_it_does: New starts a blank ANSI-footprint plate; Save/Save As… persist a custom plate; Delete removes a user plate. (Saving a bundled standard forks it to a custom name.)
settings.recommendation: Save custom plates with a clear name.

settings.name: Plate → Fit / Snap / Wheel zoom / Dim ref
settings.what_it_does: Fit (F) reframes the view; Snap toggles 1 mm drag snapping; Wheel zoom toggles scroll-wheel zoom; Dim ref (Center/Edge) chooses whether new dimensions reference the well center or its near edge.
settings.default: Snap off, Wheel zoom on, Dim ref Center
settings.recommendation: Turn Snap on for clean grid placement; Edge dim ref is handy for needle-clearance spacing.

settings.name: Rosette → designer (double-click a well to drill in) + Save plate
settings.what_it_does: Designs sub-wells inside a well; they flatten to A1.a, A1.b… and become first-class wells. Shares the plate design with the Plate page; Save plate delegates to the Plate page save (forks standards to a custom name).
settings.recommendation: Use for multi-spot inserts; edits mark the shared design dirty until you Save.

settings.name: Rosette → Rosette Library (table + Add / Edit / Remove)
settings.what_it_does: Legacy RosetteInsert preset library — Add/Edit dialog sets Name, Well format, Ring sub-wells, Center well (Yes/No), Sub-well Ø, Sub-well depth, Insert Z offset.
settings.recommendation: Optional; the in-canvas rosette designer is the primary path.

settings.name: Ink → Ink Library table + Add Ink / Edit / Remove
settings.what_it_does: Defines reagents. Add/Edit opens a dialog: Name, Well type (ink/wash/buffer/waste/oil), Ink subtype (editable presets, enabled only for 'ink'), Viscosity (cP), Granule Ø (µm), Cell Ø (µm), Density (g/mL), Color. Table shows Name/Type/Subtype/Viscosity/Granule Ø/Cell Ø.
settings.default: empty; new ink defaults viscosity 1.0 cP, density 1.0 g/mL, color #a6e3a1, granule 0, cell 0
settings.recommendation: Well type drives behavior (service-well resolution, colors); subtype is informational. Name service wells by role (wash/waste/buffer/oil) or set the matching well type.

settings.name: Ink → Reagent Locations: Reagent combo
settings.what_it_does: Selects which reagent the well clicks below assign. The combo lists every ink in the library with its type label and is colored to the ink's color.
settings.recommendation: Pick the reagent before clicking wells.

settings.name: Ink → Reagent Locations: plate view + Assign selected / Clear selected / Clear reagent
settings.what_it_does: Click wells (incl. rosette sub-wells A1.a) to select, then Assign selected pins them to the chosen reagent; Clear selected unpins the selected wells; Clear reagent removes all of this reagent's pins. Well fill = the ink's color, outline = the type color (ink/wash/waste/buffer/oil). One reagent per well.
settings.recommendation: Assign service-well locations (wash/waste/buffer/oil) here — prep/cleanup workflows resolve them from these pins, and they auto-fill the per-print Well Setup.

settings.name: Needle → Gauge
settings.what_it_does: Selects the needle gauge; info line shows ID/OD/Wall in µm. Required for a valid config.
settings.recommendation: Match the physical needle; ID drives the per-needle bore-volume used by prep/pick-place.

settings.name: Needle → Length
settings.what_it_does: Needle length (1.0"/1.5"/2.0"), used in internal-bore volume and geometry.
settings.recommendation: Set to the actual installed needle length.

settings.name: Needle → Channels
settings.what_it_does: Number of needle channels (1–3); rebuilds the channel-assignment rows.
settings.recommendation: Use >1 only for true multi-channel needles.

settings.name: Needle → Needle Channel Assignment (per-channel pump combo)
settings.what_it_does: Maps each channel to a unique enabled pump; status reads ✓ All channels assigned, or flags a duplicate/unassigned channel.
settings.recommendation: Every channel must map to a distinct enabled pump for the config to validate.

settings.name: Pump → per-pump Enable / Syringe / Mode / Inks (P1,P2,P3)
settings.what_it_does: Enable turns the pump on; Syringe sets the volume (and shows µL/mm + stroke in the info line); Mode is Incremental/Continuous; Inks is a checklist of printable inks this pump may aspirate (service reagents excluded).
settings.default: disabled; syringe — None —; mode Incremental; no inks checked
settings.recommendation: At least one pump must be enabled with a syringe and ≥1 ink for a valid config. The summary shows P1→[…] assignments.

settings.name: Pump → Pump Timing (all pumps): Settle time
settings.what_it_does: Blocking dwell held BEFORE and AFTER every discrete pump actuation (prime, aspirate, dispense, pick/place) so fluid settles before the workflow advances. Not applied to the streamed print path or manual jog.
settings.recommendation: Add a small settle (e.g. 0.1–0.5 s) for viscous inks; 0 still waits for move completion.

settings.name: Pump → Pump Timing (all pumps): Prime time
settings.what_it_does: Pre-flow lead-in duration printing workflows use to prime the needle (prime volume = flow × time). Quick Print seeds its per-run pre-flow knob from this.
settings.recommendation: Increase if prints start dry; this is the default Quick Print inherits.

settings.name: Cameras → Save Camera Settings / Load Cameras
settings.what_it_does: Save snapshots the full camera setup (sources→roles, µm/px, image correction, hardware controls, which cameras are running) as this machine's default. Load detects, restores all of that, and starts the saved cameras (same as the automatic startup restore).
settings.recommendation: Save once after a full camera setup so it auto-restores every launch.

settings.name: Cameras → Detect Cameras
settings.what_it_does: Scans for available camera sources (OpenCV / ToupCam / Simulated) and fills each slot's Source combo; auto-assigns sources from the remembered role→identity map.
settings.recommendation: Click after plugging cameras in; the count badge confirms discovery.

settings.name: Cameras → per-slot Source combo
settings.what_it_does: Picks which detected camera plays this slot. Applies it to the live manager so Start opens this slot's camera; restores that camera's stored µm/px and remembers the role→identity.
settings.recommendation: Assign before Start; the assignment auto-restores next session by device identity.

settings.name: Cameras → per-slot Role combo (Unassigned / Microscope / Needle X-view / Needle Y-view)
settings.what_it_does: Tags the slot's workflow role. Microscope/Needle X/Needle Y are singletons — assigning one clears it from any other slot. Roles drive the rest of the page and the calibration tabs.
settings.recommendation: Assign Microscope to the overhead-objective camera and Needle X/Y to the two side cameras.

settings.name: Cameras → per-slot ▶ Start / ⏹ Stop + live preview
settings.what_it_does: Powers the slot's camera on/off via the shared manager and shows a live preview so you can verify the feed. Disabled until a source is picked.
settings.recommendation: Start the camera before running its µm/px calibration.

settings.name: Cameras → per-slot Image Correction sliders (Brightness / Contrast / Gamma + Reset)
settings.what_it_does: Per-slot display-only correction pushed live to the manager; persisted per device identity on slider release. Reset returns to neutral.
settings.recommendation: Display-only — does not affect the raw frame used for detection/calibration; tune for a clear preview.

settings.name: Cameras → Microscope Camera Setup: Camera spec
settings.what_it_does: Picks the microscope camera model (sensor spec). Selecting one repopulates the Resolution combo.
settings.recommendation: Pick the model that matches the assigned microscope camera.

settings.name: Cameras → Microscope Camera Setup: Resolution
settings.what_it_does: Active capture resolution; changing it on a live microscope also drives the device to the nearest supported mode.
settings.default: Lowest resolution selected when a spec is picked
settings.recommendation: Changing capture resolution may require redoing µm/px — the app logs a warning.

settings.name: Cameras → Microscope Camera Setup: Installed objective (read-only)
settings.what_it_does: Mirrors the objective chosen in Objective Calibration Setup; drives the spec-computed magnification.
settings.recommendation: Set it via the 'Currently installed' combo in Objective Calibration Setup below.

settings.name: Cameras → Microscope Camera Setup: Pixel scale / Override (Use custom scale + µm/px)
settings.what_it_does: Shows the active µm/px; ticking 'Use custom scale' enables a manual µm/px spin that overrides the computed value.
settings.recommendation: Prefer a measured objective calibration; use the override only as a fallback.

settings.name: Cameras → Microscope Camera Setup: Field of view (read-only)
settings.what_it_does: Displays the computed field of view from resolution × µm/px.
settings.recommendation: A sanity check that the scale is plausible.

settings.name: Cameras → Needle Cameras Setup: Calibrate µm/px… (X-view / Y-view)
settings.what_it_does: Launches the stage-motion µm/px calibration for that needle camera (move the stage a known distance, correlate pixel displacement). Disabled until that role is assigned; requires the camera started and the stage connected.
settings.recommendation: Calibrate both side cameras; the card shows the measured µm/px (and rotation) once done.

settings.name: Cameras → Objective Calibration Setup: Currently installed combo
settings.what_it_does: Selects the mounted objective; pushes its stored µm/px (and rotation) into the live pipeline on swap.
settings.recommendation: Switch this whenever you physically change objectives.

settings.name: Cameras → Objective Calibration Setup: Add Objective… / Remove Selected
settings.what_it_does: Add opens a dialog (Name + nominal magnification) to define a user objective; Remove deletes it and its calibrations on every camera (confirm).
settings.default: empty library; Add dialog defaults nominal 4.0×
settings.recommendation: Define one entry per physical objective; the nominal mag only seeds spec-computed µm/px until you calibrate.

settings.name: Cameras → Objective Calibration Setup: Calibrate Selected… / Clear Calibration
settings.what_it_does: Calibrate runs the stage-motion PixelCalibrationDialog and stores the measured µm/px per objective (needs the microscope started + stage connected). Clear removes the stored value (falls back to spec-computed).
settings.recommendation: Calibrate each objective you use; a ⚠ on the Date column means it was calibrated at a different resolution than active.

settings.name: Xbox Controller sub-page
settings.what_it_does: Dedicated Xbox controller setup (mapping editor, jog-speed read-outs, deadzones/offsets). Shares state with the Connect Hardware panel's Xbox row.
settings.recommendation: Optional — only needed if you jog with an Xbox controller.

settings.name: Actions → Save Config / Load Config
settings.what_it_does: Save writes the current hardware config to disk (config/hardware/); Load reads a previously saved hardware config.
settings.recommendation: Save once the Setup Status reads ✓ Setup complete.

settings.name: Setup Status banner
settings.what_it_does: Live validity readout: ⚠ lines list each missing requirement; ✓ Setup complete means the config validates and all sidebar pages unlock.
settings.recommendation: This is the gate — resolve every ⚠ line to unlock the rest of the app.

safety_notes: The setup-mode jog pad on Hardware Setup BYPASSES soft-limit clamping AND the pump-enabled check (a yellow banner warns of this) so you can reach mechanical extremes — drive carefully; the needle/plate are not protected here. Watch the Live Position bars: markers ring red past the recorded envelope.

On ME3B V1 the needle descends as raw Z increases. Do the Z Axis Setup (Set Bottom while fully DOWN, Set Top while fully UP) so the up-direction is derived correctly; a wrong assumption can drive the needle into the plate. If Bottom/Top are too close the status warns the direction is ambiguous — jog further apart and re-run.

The Z soft-limit envelope is owned by Device → Z Axis Setup / Save Safety Limits & Zero. After recording min/max, Save so the live controller clamps real moves; with 'Enable safety limits' off, nothing clamps anywhere in the app.

Pump Plunger Setup DERIVES and OWNS the aspirate/dispense direction. Only confirm 2 · Set Aspirated when the plunger is truly empty→full. A wrong derived sign reverses fluid flow — re-run per machine after any pump wiring change.

Override / Sync Axis Position sends G92 to rebase Marlin's counter (no motion) — only use it to recover position after a ZP power cycle, in the zero-referenced mm frame (not the raw counter shown in the limit rows).

Changing the 'Plate mounted 180°' checkbox or the plate format/custom plate invalidates the taught XY plate calibration — re-teach plate calibration on the Calibration page afterward, or motion will drive to a mirrored/garbage well.

Inverting an axis (ZP Stage Calibration → Invert Direction, or a negative steps/mm, or a clicked steps/mm cell) flips Marlin's positive direction permanently for that axis; verify jog direction afterward.
Marlin loses absolute position on power-cycle; if the ZP board was power-cycled the readout may be wrong until you Override/Sync or re-run the Z setup.

Calibrating capture resolution changes µm/px validity — the app warns that µm/px may need redoing after a resolution change; a ⚠ on an objective's Date column means it was calibrated at a different resolution than the active one.

The config is invalid (sidebar stays locked) until a needle gauge is set, ≥1 pump is enabled with a syringe and an ink, the plate format/custom plate is recognized, and each needle channel maps to a unique enabled pump — the Setup Status banner names exactly what is missing.
tips: The Connect Hardware + Jog Stages + Live Position panel is the same panel on every sub-page (left edge) — you never lose access to jogging or position while configuring other sections. Its sections are collapsible cards.
Sub-pages are ordered so each builds on the one to its left: Device → Identity → Plate → Rosette → Ink → Needle → Pump → Cameras → Xbox. Work left to right the first time.

Camera µm/px, objective calibrations, image correction, and role→camera assignments live in a per-machine store keyed by device identity (USB port + name), so they survive loading a different setup file and restarts — they are NOT inside the swappable hardware config.
Device → Device Profile is the fastest way to restore a whole machine: Load applies safety limits, feedrates, axis map, steps/mm, Z setup, plate orientation, and pump calibration in one click.

Per-section Save buttons (Save Mapping, Save XY Calibration, Save Calibration, Save Feedrates, Save Safety Limits & Zero, Save offsets) each persist their own section; the bottom Apply Settings commits the whole Device page at once.

The per-pump Inks checklist only lists printable inks — wash/waste/buffer/oil are filtered out (by well type or by an ink named one of those roles), so you can't accidentally aspirate a service reagent.
Pump Plunger Setup blocks live on the Device sub-page right beneath the Z Axis Setup, in order Z, P1, P2, P3 — not on the Pump sub-page (that one has Enable/Syringe/Mode/Inks + Pump Timing).
If a Cameras button seems to do nothing, the camera may not be Started — Calibrate µm/px and objective calibration both require the relevant camera running and the stage connected.

guides.title: Calibration
guides.overview: The Calibration page teaches the machine three things it needs before printing or running any workflow: where the needle tip sits (Needle Location), how high the needle can travel and where the plate surfaces are (Needle Offset Calibration / Z reference heights), and where each well is in stage XY (Plate Location) plus how deep each well bottom is (Plate Z Auto-Cal). It is organized as five tabs in left-to-right order: Needle Location, Needle Offset Calibration, Plate Location, Plate Z Auto-Cal, and Custom (power-user wizards). An operator works left to right: center the needle, capture the safe/travel and plate heights, map the wells, then find each well bottom by focus. A "Use last known location" shortcut and a "Re-derive wells from saved mosaic" shortcut let you skip the long workflows when nothing has physically changed.
guides.where_to_find: Sidebar → Calibration page. Tabs across the top, left to right: Needle Location, Needle Offset Calibration, Plate Location, Plate Z Auto-Cal, Custom.
prerequisites: Hardware Setup → Cameras: assign the Needle X-view and Needle Y-view roles to the two side cameras (the Needle Location camera tiles stay as placeholders until both NEEDLE_X / NEEDLE_Y roles are assigned), and assign the Microscope role to the overhead camera (needed for Plate Location auto edge-detect, the mosaic scan, and Plate Z Auto-Cal focus).

Hardware Setup → Cameras: calibrate µm/pixel for the microscope objective. Plate Location well edge-fit, the mosaic scan, and the needle-offset preview refuse to run on an uncalibrated camera (the Run handler explicitly blocks with 'Microscope camera µm/pixel not calibrated').
Stage controller connected (XY + ZP). Many actions warn 'Stage controller required' / 'not connected' if missing.
Hardware Setup → Device: set the Z soft-limit envelope (z_min/z_max). The calibration tab no longer owns it — capturing Max Z / Plate Bottom Z here does NOT change the safety envelope.

Hardware Setup → Cameras: select the microscope objective in use — when wells are queued, the Plate Location Run is blocked by a 'Confirm objective' dialog if no objective is selected, and you must answer Yes that the scope is physically set to that objective.

Order matters: capture the Fast Move (Safe) Z on the Needle Offset Calibration tab BEFORE running Plate Location, a Mosaic scan, 'Go to needle location', or Plate Z Auto-Cal whenever the ZP/needle is connected — those steps retract the needle to the Safe Z, and with no Safe Z the retract would fall back to zero-ref 0 (the bottom datum = a crash).

steps.title: Center the needle (Needle Location tab)
steps.detail: Open Needle Location. The X-view and Y-view side cameras appear at top (placeholders until the NEEDLE_X / NEEDLE_Y roles are assigned in Hardware Setup → Cameras). Jog the needle into both views. The wizard walks 4 steps in order: click the tip's left edge in X-view, the right edge in X-view, then the left and right edges in Y-view. Each click is logged in the 4-row pick table (X-view left/right, Y-view left/right) and the step banner advances.

steps.title: Review the offset preview and save the needle origin
steps.detail: Once all four edges are picked, 'Offset preview' shows the computed ΔX/ΔY (and ΔZ if 'Also center Z' is on) plus a per-camera column-offset breakdown. Click 'Center & Save needle origin' — the stage moves XY (and optionally Z) to put the tip on both crosshairs, captures the post-move XY as needle_origin_um (label turns green), saves the absolute XY as the quick-move location, and records the needle-cam Z fiducial. If the crosshair already sits WITHIN the needle's width in both views, it records the origin WITHOUT moving (a deadband against click-noise). Use 'Reset picks' to start the four clicks over.

steps.title: (Optional) skip re-centering when nothing changed
steps.detail: If the needle, its mounting, and the side cameras are unchanged since last session, click '✓ Use last known location'. It restores the saved needle reference (needle zero + needle-cam Z + saved needle XY) read straight from settings, software-only — NO stage motion. Then verify with '⤵ Go to needle location' and only re-center if it looks off. On a brand-new machine, use 'Set current as location' once to seed the quick-move before the first Center & Save.

steps.title: Capture the Z reference heights (Needle Offset Calibration tab)
steps.detail: Open Needle Offset Calibration. Jog Z to each reference height and click its 'Set …' button to capture the current Z: Replace Z (needle-swap clearance), Max Z (upper print reference), Fast Move Z (travel height — REQUIRED before Plate Location), Plate Top Z (plate surface), Plate Bottom Z (well floor). Each label turns green with the saved mm value. Optionally click 'Estimate plate Z (pre-fill guesses)' to pre-fill Plate Top / Plate Bottom / Fast-Move Z from the needle-cam fiducial minus the standard offsets (Max/Replace are left manual). 'Go to Replace Z' retracts Z to the captured swap height (XY stays put).

steps.title: Map the wells in XY (Plate Location tab)
steps.detail: Open Plate Location. Choose the Well-fit mode: 'Manual — click well edge in live view' (default) or 'Auto — camera edge-detect'. Use the Free/Snap toggle on the plate view to enqueue targets: Snap = click wells, Free = click anywhere to drop a freeform point (clicking an already-queued well/point removes it). Queue several wells spread across the plate, then click 'Run'. If the ZP is connected and you have not set the Fast Move Z, Run is blocked with a warning — go set it first.

steps.title: Teach each well during the run
steps.detail: When wells are queued, you must first confirm the in-use objective (a dialog that blocks if none is selected). The stage then retracts to Safe Z once and travels to each queued target. In Manual mode, JOG to bring each rim edge into the microscope view and click the well EDGE (each click records a rim point at the CURRENT stage position — the stage is never driven by a click); collect ~3+ points (8 suggested) around the rim, then click 'Confirm position' to circle-fit the center (needs ≥3 valid points). In Auto mode the camera edge-detects automatically and falls back to a manual 3-point pick if it fails. For freeform points, jog to center the target and Confirm. 'Skip' leaves a well/point uncalibrated and advances; 'Cancel run' aborts and discards results. Taught well centers show as pink reference markers on the plate and microscope views.

steps.title: (Alternative) full-plate mosaic scan
steps.detail: Instead of clicking each well, click 'Mosaic scan' in the Mosaic group to raster the whole plate (needle retracted to Safe Z), stitch one composite image on a worker thread, and detect every well at once. Tune it via 'Settings…' (camera settle/timing, FOV overlap, resolution, detection sensitivity). 'Calibrate…' builds a small mosaic to estimate and store this camera+objective's alignment delta. 'Map wells…' lets you place the 3 corner wells by hand on the stitched mosaic and auto-place the rest. 'Quick re-register' re-fits the whole plate from a saved template by visiting only 3 reference wells. 'Scan well…' maps the sub-wells of one rosette well. Use the 'Plate view' combo (Ideal well / Mosaic / Mosaic + well) and the 'Manual align' sliders + 'Re-anchor map (1 point)…' to verify and correct registration by eye.

steps.title: (Shortcut) re-derive wells after a plate-orientation change
steps.detail: If the plate orientation changed and the saved map is mirrored/stale, click 'Re-derive wells from saved mosaic (ground truth)'. It re-labels every well from the saved mosaic's detected centers for the current orientation and stores them directly as the calibration, discarding the old taught/warp state. This is software-only — NO stage motion.

steps.title: Find each well bottom (Plate Z Auto-Cal tab)
steps.detail: Open Plate Z Auto-Cal (it comes after Plate Location because it drives to the mapped wells). Click 'Start Z Auto-Cal'. Start validates that a plate is selected, Fast Move Z and Plate Top Z are set, the XY map (Plate Location) is finished, and a camera is running. For each calibration well (A1, A-last-col, last-row-last-col) the stage retracts and travels there. Focus the microscope on the glass with the manual knob, then click 'Confirm focus & lower needle' — the needle lowers (coarse 0.15 mm then fine 0.03 mm steps) and the best-focus Z (sharpest needle circle = tip at glass) is recorded. Click 'Accept & next well' to keep it, or 'Redo well' to re-teach. Use 'Record now' to manually capture the current Z if auto-detect picks the wrong frame. After the last well the Z plane (tilt) is fit. 'Cancel' stops and retracts to Safe Z.

steps.title: Retract the needle safely while teaching (Z side view)
steps.detail: On the Plate Location tab, the 'Z side view' panel (right of the plate map) shows the needle height. Click the green 'Safe' badge to drive Z up to the captured Fast Move Z — a manual absolute Z move that respects soft limits and is a no-op if the ZP stage is not connected — before or while teaching wells, so a needle you jogged down to focus is lifted clear of the plate.

settings.name: X-view / Y-view camera tiles (Needle Location)
settings.what_it_does: Live feeds from the two side cameras assigned the NEEDLE_X and NEEDLE_Y roles, with a crosshair. Clicking inside a tile records the needle tip's edge for the current wizard step. Each shows a placeholder until both roles are assigned in Hardware Setup → Cameras.
settings.recommendation: Jog the needle into BOTH views before clicking. Click the actual tip edges, not the shaft.

settings.name: ⤵ Go to needle location
settings.what_it_does: Quick-moves to the saved approximate needle location: retracts Z to the Fast-Move height, travels XY, then lowers to the saved needle-cam Z so the needle re-enters both side views. Warns if no location is saved or the stage isn't connected; refuses (warns) if ZP is connected and no Fast Move (Safe) Z is set.
settings.recommendation: Use to bring the needle back into the side cameras instead of hand-jogging.

settings.name: Set current as location
settings.what_it_does: Captures the current stage XY as the approximate needle location (the quick-move target). Persisted per machine. Warns if the stage isn't connected or the position can't be read.
settings.recommendation: Use once on a fresh machine to seed the quick-move before your first Center & Save.

settings.name: ✓ Use last known location
settings.what_it_does: Restores the last-known needle calibration (needle zero + needle-cam Z + saved needle XY) read from settings, software-only with no stage motion. Lets you skip the camera re-centering entirely.
settings.recommendation: ONLY use when nothing about the needle, its mounting, or the side cameras has changed since it was saved — otherwise the needle reference will be wrong.

settings.name: Also center Z (tip → crosshair) [checkbox]
settings.what_it_does: When checked, after recentering XY the needle Z is moved so the tip's center-bottom lands on the camera crosshair. The move is clamped by the Z soft-limit (move_z_user_relative). The ΔZ is shown in the offset preview.
settings.recommendation: Leave on for a full center.

settings.name: Invert Z direction (flipped camera mount) [checkbox]
settings.what_it_does: Flips the sign of the Z-centering move for vertically-mirrored camera mounts.
settings.recommendation: Toggle only if the Z move drives the tip AWAY from the crosshair instead of toward it.

settings.name: Reset picks
settings.what_it_does: Clears all four edge picks and returns the wizard to step 1.
settings.recommendation: Use if you mis-clicked an edge.

settings.name: Center & Save needle origin
settings.what_it_does: Drives the stage to put the needle on both crosshairs (XY and optional Z), then saves the current stage position as needle_origin_um, the quick-move XY, and the needle-cam Z fiducial. Disabled until all four edges are picked. Skips the XY move if the crosshair already lies within the needle width in both views (deadband).
settings.recommendation: Review the offset preview first; large offsets will produce a real move.

settings.name: Set Replace Z
settings.what_it_does: Captures the current Z (zero-ref) as the needle-swap clearance height — the highest safe Z used when changing the needle. Kept as a reference; does not change the safety envelope.
settings.recommendation: Jog Z to your comfortable needle-swap height first, then capture.

settings.name: Set Max Z
settings.what_it_does: Captures the current Z as the upper print/Z reference (stored in self._max_z). NOTE: despite its tooltip saying 'soft-limit ceiling', in this version it does NOT write into the Z safety envelope — that is owned by Hardware Setup → Device. (The old behavior could invert the envelope and freeze Z.)
settings.recommendation: Optional reference. Set the actual soft-limit ceiling on Hardware Setup → Device.

settings.name: Set Fast Move Z
settings.what_it_does: Captures the current Z as the travel height for fast XY moves between wells (retract-before-XY height). This is the Safe Z the Plate Location run, Mosaic scan, Go-to-needle, and Plate Z Auto-Cal retract to. Stored as self._safe_z.
settings.recommendation: REQUIRED before running Plate Location / Mosaic scan / Plate Z Auto-Cal when the ZP is connected. Set it well above the tallest plate feature.

settings.name: Set Plate Top Z
settings.what_it_does: Captures the current Z as the plate's top surface (first contact from above). Pushed to the controller as the plate-top datum for printing. Required before Plate Z Auto-Cal.
settings.recommendation: Jog the needle just touching the plate top, then capture.

settings.name: Set Plate Bottom Z
settings.what_it_does: Captures the current Z as the well floor (needle just touching the bottom of a calibrated well, stored in self._plate_bottom_z). Kept as a print/Z reference; does not change the safety envelope. Used as a fallback reference for the Z auto-cal descent window.
settings.recommendation: Capture against a known well bottom; the Z auto-cal refines per-well.

settings.name: Estimate plate Z (pre-fill guesses)
settings.what_it_does: Pre-fills Plate Top / Plate Bottom / Fast-Move Z with guesses derived from the captured needle-cam Z minus the standard offsets set on Hardware Setup → Device. Max/Replace Z are left untouched. Warns if no needle-cam Z has been captured.
settings.recommendation: Run a needle Center & Save first (records the needle-cam Z), then use this to seed the heights and refine them.

settings.name: Go to Replace Z
settings.what_it_does: Drives Z to the captured Replace Z for needle swapping (absolute Z move via move_z_absolute; XY stays put). Information popup if Replace Z is not set; returns silently if the controller is missing.
settings.recommendation: Use before physically changing the needle.

settings.name: Well fit mode combo (Plate Location)
settings.what_it_does: Chooses how each queued well is centered during a run. 'Manual — click well edge in live view': the stage anchors at the predicted center, you jog and click the rim edge in the microscope feed (≥3 clicks → circle fit). 'Auto — camera edge-detect': automatic detection with a manual 3-point fallback.
settings.default: Manual — click well edge in live view
settings.recommendation: Manual is the most reliable when wells are larger than the field of view or detection is noisy.

settings.name: Plate view + Free/Snap toggle
settings.what_it_does: Top-down workspace view (same JogWorkspaceView as the Jog page): safety envelope, plate outline, wells colored by calibrated/approximate status, needle to scale, and pink reference markers for taught centers. The built-in Free/Snap toggle (top-left of the view) routes clicks: Snap = click wells to enqueue, Free = click anywhere to drop a freeform point. Clicking an already-queued well/point removes it.
settings.recommendation: Mix Snap (wells) and Free (arbitrary points), then Run.

settings.name: Microscope live feed (Plate Location)
settings.what_it_does: Live microscope camera feed (with crosshair) under the plate map. In Manual well-fit, clicking the well edge here records a rim point at the current stage position (converted to absolute µm via the calibrated µm/px). Starts on Run / Mosaic scan or from the Cameras tab.
settings.recommendation: Spread your rim clicks around the whole circle for a good fit.

settings.name: Mosaic (live) preview
settings.what_it_does: Shows the stitched mosaic building tile-by-tile during a Mosaic scan (worker thread), and any previously-saved mosaic for the plate.
settings.default: 'No mosaic yet — run a Mosaic scan'

settings.name: Target queue list + Clear queue + Run
settings.what_it_does: Lists queued wells and freeform points. 'Clear queue' empties it. 'Run' starts the calibration run (disabled until there is something to run; also blocked if no plate/controller, if Fast Move Z is unset with ZP connected, or if wells are queued and the microscope camera/µm-px isn't ready).
settings.default: Run disabled until queue has entries
settings.recommendation: Queue several wells spread across the plate for an accurate XY fit.

settings.name: Mosaic scan
settings.what_it_does: Rasters the whole plate (needle retracted to Safe Z), stitches every snapshot into one image on a worker thread, then detects all wells at once on the stitched field. Robust where single-frame per-well detection fails.
settings.recommendation: Use for a fresh full-plate map. Requires a calibrated microscope µm/px and a Microscope-role camera.

settings.name: Settings… (Mosaic)
settings.what_it_does: Opens the mosaic-scan settings dialog: camera settle/timing, FOV overlap, mosaic resolution, and well-detection sensitivity/tolerance. Persisted in settings.json.
settings.recommendation: Increase camera settle if the camera can't keep up during the raster.

settings.name: Calibrate… (Mosaic)
settings.what_it_does: Opens the alignment calibration pop-out: build a small (e.g. 5×5) mosaic you define, run global registration to estimate this camera + objective's alignment delta, and store it so full mosaics start pre-registered.

settings.name: Map wells…
settings.what_it_does: Maps wells on the stitched mosaic by hand: click the 3 corner wells, the rest auto-place from the plate layout, drag to refine, then confirm. Also saves the labeled mosaic for detection R&D.
settings.recommendation: Good fallback when automatic well detection mis-labels wells.

settings.name: Quick re-register
settings.what_it_does: Re-registers the plate from a saved mosaic template: the camera drives to 3 reference wells, auto-detects each, and fits the whole plate — no full re-scan. Needs the SAME camera + objective.
settings.recommendation: Use when you remounted a previously-scanned plate and just need to re-lock the map.

settings.name: Scan well…
settings.what_it_does: Builds a high-resolution mosaic of one rosette well and maps its sub-wells (uses the plate's sub-well layout).
settings.recommendation: Only for plates with rosette sub-wells.

settings.name: Re-derive wells from saved mosaic (ground truth)
settings.what_it_does: Re-labels every well from the saved mosaic's detected centers for the current plate orientation and stores them directly as the calibration, discarding the previous taught/warp calibration. Software-only — NO stage motion.
settings.recommendation: Use after the plate orientation changed (e.g. the map became mirrored). Discards prior calibration, so be sure.

settings.name: Plate view combo (Ideal well / Mosaic / Mosaic + well)
settings.what_it_does: Switches the plate map between the idealized well grid, the stitched plate mosaic, or both overlaid.
settings.recommendation: Use 'Mosaic + well' to visually verify the well map registers to the real plate image.

settings.name: Re-anchor map (1 point)…
settings.what_it_does: Fallback for a mis-registered map: pick a well/point on the plate overview (the stage travels there), then click that same feature in the live microscope view. The measured offset re-anchors the ENTIRE well map (a pure translation) and is saved permanently.
settings.recommendation: Use when the whole map is shifted by a constant offset that auto re-register can't fix.

settings.name: Manual align group (Δx µm / Δy µm / Opacity sliders + Store / Reset / Clear stored)
settings.what_it_does: Checkable group to slide the stitched mosaic onto the well grid by eye. Δx/Δy sliders range ±10000 µm; Opacity 5–100% (default 55%). 'Store alignment' saves the shift as this camera+objective's alignment delta (added to any prior) and bakes it into the saved overlay. 'Reset' clears the live sliders. 'Clear stored' forgets the stored delta so auto registration sets it next scan.
settings.recommendation: Use only when auto registration can't lock on (featureless tiles). Store once you have it aligned by eye.

settings.name: Confirm position / Skip / Cancel run (Plate Location, shown only while paused)
settings.what_it_does: These three buttons are hidden until the run pauses at a target. Confirm = fit/record the current paused target (a freeform point, a well's 3-point pick, or the click-rim edges collected so far). Skip = leave the current well/point uncalibrated and advance. Cancel run = abort the whole run and discard results.
settings.recommendation: Confirm needs ≥3 valid rim points for a manual/edge-fit well; otherwise it warns and leaves the well uncalibrated.

settings.name: Z side view + green 'Safe' badge (Plate Location)
settings.what_it_does: Shows the needle height on a vertical scale plus the captured Z references. Clicking the green 'Safe' badge drives Z up to the Fast Move Z (move_z_absolute, soft limits respected). No-op when the ZP stage is not connected.
settings.recommendation: Click it before/while teaching wells to lift a lowered needle clear of the plate.

settings.name: Start Z Auto-Cal / Cancel (Plate Z Auto-Cal)
settings.what_it_does: Start begins the guided per-well Z-bottom calibration. It validates that a plate is selected, Fast Move Z and Plate Top Z are set, the XY map (Plate Location) is finished, and a camera is running — warning and aborting if any is missing. Cancel stops the run, retracts to Safe Z, and stops detection.
settings.default: Cancel disabled until a run starts
settings.recommendation: Finish Plate Location first; the auto-cal drives to the mapped wells.

settings.name: Confirm focus & lower needle (Plate Z Auto-Cal)
settings.what_it_does: Tells the system the microscope is focused on the glass at the current well. The needle then lowers (coarse 0.15 mm then fine 0.03 mm steps) within a bounded, soft-limited window to find the sharpest-focus Z (tip at the glass plane).
settings.default: enabled only while awaiting focus confirmation
settings.recommendation: Focus crisply on the glass with the manual knob first — that defines the search baseline.

settings.name: Record now (Plate Z Auto-Cal)
settings.what_it_does: Manual override during the descent: records the current best-focus Z (or the live Z if none seen yet) as this well's bottom.
settings.default: enabled only during the coarse/fine descent
settings.recommendation: Use if the auto peak-finder picks the wrong frame.

settings.name: Accept & next well / Redo well (Plate Z Auto-Cal)
settings.what_it_does: Accept keeps the provisional best-focus Z for this well, advances to the next, and (after the last well) fits the Z plane / tilt. Redo discards the provisional Z and re-arms the focus gate so you re-teach this well.
settings.default: enabled only once a Z is recorded
settings.recommendation: Redo if the recorded value looks wrong (e.g. 'no clear focus peak').

settings.name: Live microscope feed (Plate Z Auto-Cal)
settings.what_it_does: Passive microscope feed (with crosshair) for watching the needle approach focus while teaching. Starts automatically when this tab is shown.

settings.name: Well depth spin (Custom → Plate Calibration, Step 2)
settings.what_it_does: Well depth in mm (range 1.0–50.0, default 17.4; tooltip 'Distance from plate top surface to well bottom glass'). Auto-populated from the selected plate. Seeds the fallback search window for the per-well Z descent when no previous accepted Z and no Plate Bottom Z exist.
settings.recommendation: Auto-populated from the selected plate; usually leave as-is.

settings.name: Custom tab → Camera Setup / Full Wizard / Plate Calibration sub-tabs
settings.what_it_does: Power-user area: a live multi-camera grid plus the full legacy wizards — Camera Setup, the complete needle wizard (Full Wizard), and manual plate calibration (Plate Calibration: plate-format combo, per-well manual Z teach, edge-finding, the well-depth spin, and Z-plane tilt fit).
settings.recommendation: Use only when the streamlined workflow tabs don't cover a manual step you need.

safety_notes: Set the Fast Move (Safe) Z on the Needle Offset Calibration tab BEFORE running Plate Location, a Mosaic scan, 'Go to needle location', or Plate Z Auto-Cal whenever the ZP/needle is connected. Those steps retract the needle to that Safe Z; without it the retract would fall back to zero-ref 0 (the bottom datum on this machine = a crash). The Run, Go-to-needle, and Start-Z-Auto-Cal handlers are explicitly gated and will warn you.

The Plate Location run retracts the needle to Safe Z ONCE before the scan and again before every inter-well/inter-point hop (via ensure_retracted_to / safe_travel_to, which never descend), so a needle you jogged down to focus is lifted before the stage travels.

Plate Z Auto-Cal lowers the needle toward the glass under a bounded, soft-limit-clamped descent window; it stops at the focus peak or the safety floor and never descends past the window. Cancel and the per-well flow retract to Safe Z.

Capturing Max Z and Plate Bottom Z on the Needle Offset tab does NOT change the Z safety envelope (it's owned by Hardware Setup → Device), even though Max Z's tooltip still reads 'soft-limit ceiling'. This is intentional — the old behavior could invert the envelope and freeze Z. Set the real soft limits on the Device page.

'Use last known location' and 'Re-derive wells from saved mosaic' are software-only (no motion) — but they overwrite the live needle/plate calibration, so only use them when you are sure the physical setup is unchanged (last-known) or the orientation truly changed (re-derive discards the previous taught/warp calibration).

The green 'Safe' badge and 'Go to Replace Z' issue real Z moves; they only act when the ZP stage is connected and respect Z soft limits. 'Go to needle location' performs a full retract→XY→lower travel and is gated on a known Safe Z when ZP is connected.

When wells are queued, the Plate Location Run is blocked by a 'Confirm objective' dialog if no objective is selected, and you must confirm the scope is physically set to that objective — the wrong objective's µm/px would map your clicks to the wrong stage positions.

Plate Location well edge-fit and the mosaic scan refuse to run on an uncalibrated microscope µm/px (the Run handler warns 'Microscope camera µm/pixel not calibrated'); calibrate the objective in Hardware Setup → Cameras first.
tips: Work the tabs left to right: Needle Location → Needle Offset Calibration (capture at least Fast Move Z + Plate Top Z) → Plate Location → Plate Z Auto-Cal.

In Plate Location Manual mode, every live-view click uses the stage's CURRENT position, so jog freely between clicks — the stage is never driven by a click. Spread ~8 clicks around the whole rim for the best circle fit (≥3 minimum).
Calibration changes auto-save (debounced) so you won't lose a taught Safe Z / Top Z / well centers if you forget to save manually.
The pink reference markers on the plate map and microscope view mark your taught well centers — use them to confirm the map registers to the real plate.

If a Mosaic-scan or Re-derive button seems to do nothing, check the terminal/log: those handlers are wrapped to surface errors, but a stuck busy flag means another run is in progress — Cancel it first (Run is also blocked while a mosaic scan owns the stage).
The Z Auto-Cal calibrates 3 wells forming a right triangle (A1, A-last-column, last-row-last-column) to fit the plate tilt plane; you don't have to teach every well's bottom.
